environment: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300 x64, MSVC 14.51.36231 (Visual Studio 18 Community), CMake 4.4.4, loopback 127.0.0.1
game_exe_sha256: N/A (prototype does not touch the game)
errors: B: host packets_in=0; clients connect_timeout. Earlier: host exit 2 'cannot open log file' (fopen_s sharing).
objective: Explain an E2E run where the host received 0 packets and both clients failed with connect_timeout.
hypothesis: Freshly linked executables start late on first launch (likely an antivirus scan), so the clients' 5 s connect window can expire before the host listens, or vice versa.
procedure: A/B/C: ./scripts/test.ps1 -E2E without rebuild, right after deleting+relinking both executables, and again. Then relink + warm-up (each binary run 1 s on port 47812) + E2E, 2 valid trials.
expected_result: Joins later than usual right after a relink; normal on subsequent runs.
observed_result: Original failure reproduced on 2026-10-23 (review #1 work): (A) E2E without rebuild PASSED; (B) E2E immediately after relinking mordor-host.exe/mordor-client.exe FAILED with host packets_in=0 although host_started was logged and the clients ran concurrently, so a late process start is NOT the cause (the earlier hypothesis is contradicted); (C) the next run PASSED. No Windows Firewall rules reference these executables (read-only check). After a relink, a 1 s warm-up run of each binary before the E2E avoided the failure in 2 of 2 trials (one manual, one via test.ps1; a third scripted attempt aborted before the E2E on a PowerShell stderr error and is not counted). Root cause remains UNKNOWN (likely environmental: first-run inspection of new binaries by security software; not verified). Separately found and fixed: the previous mitigation was invalid because test.ps1 polled the previous run's host.log, and fopen_s opened logs exclusively so a concurrent reader made the host fail with 'cannot open log file'.
follow_up: Keep the warm-up step in test.ps1. If it recurs, inspect the Windows Defender operational event log (needs user approval).
